fixes.explanation: The Jordan it is, friend! The LORD says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.” Moses, Israel's leader, has died, and the LORD tells Joshua, “Now therefore arise, you and all these people…” Big news, and I'd still need a minute to stretch before a morning like that.

I see why that sounds right, but the LORD says otherwise. He tells Joshua, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So the LORD is pointing back to a promise He had already made.

False is right, friend, and the clue is two little words: “just as.” The LORD says, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. That promise has a history, so it's no fresh batch.

Moses, Israel's leader, is the name the LORD gives. He says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” Joshua is called Moses' assistant in the first verse, so he knows this man well. And then the LORD adds, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

Judging disputes? Not in this passage, friend. The LORD gives the reason for courage plainly: “…you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.” Joshua's job is handing over a promise, and that takes nerve all by itself.

Careful, friend, that statement is in the text. The LORD says, “Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.” So True was the answer here. No swerving either way.

Day and night, friend. The LORD says, “This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night…” That's no once-in-a-while thing. I can barely keep a batch from burning, so I'm impressed.

Winter isn't in this message, friend. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross the Jordan…” So the people are to get provisions ready, because the crossing is coming within three days.

Moab's army? Nobody's invited to that meeting, friend. Joshua says they will cross “…to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.” The LORD is giving the land, and that's why they go.

True, friend. Joshua says, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. Notice the word “may,” because Joshua is giving them permission. The mighty men of valor have a different job.

That statement is actually in the text. Joshua tells those tribes, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So True was the answer, and the key word is “may.”

Close, but that's not the job for the mighty men of valor. Joshua says the wives, young children and livestock “may remain” in the land Moses gave them. The mighty men “must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” So they head across first.
